## Kuranov total bubble pressures on published observation sets (#422)

The #411 MDEA model gives **19.5292% average absolute relative deviation (AARD)** on Kuranov et al. (1996), Table 2, close to the **19.7%** Wangler et al. reported on 82 unfitted pressures. The #411 fit used 70 of these pressures (66 loaded and four CO₂-free). The 12 unfitted pressures give 22.0884% AARD. The data roles differ across the models, so these deviations provide no ranking. Uyan et al. reported 22.9% on 82 pressures in Table 6. Wangler et al. redetermined that value as 34.4% in Table 11, note b. The identification of the 82 points with Kuranov's Table 2 rests on the source, count and, for Uyan, the stated concentrations and ranges. [Study definitions and source locators](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/422).

The measured quantity is total pressure at the first stable bubble, over about 313–413 K. K19 and K32 are the two Table 2 blocks, at nominal 19 and 32 wt% MDEA. K19-loaded selects the 39 rows at $\alpha>0.01$. Five K82 rows exceed $\alpha=1.2$. C28 selects the loaded K19 rows at nominal 333–413 K, and C21 applies the 3 MPa bound. Cleeton et al. report 20.26% AAD for 26 unidentified observations at 18.9 wt% (Table 3 and discussion of Fig. 7). Seven C28 rows exceed 3 MPa (18, 26, 27, 33, 34, 40 and 41), so C28 and C21 provide comparisons at the corresponding concentration and temperature range. [Retained row membership and full-precision reductions](results/kuranov-published-422/statistics.json).

The 81 retained #411 predictions replayed with zero relative difference on Engine 1.3.1. Row 72, at 393.16 K and 0.373385 mol CO₂/mol MDEA, gives 1.705047 MPa against 1.205300 MPa measured (+41.46%) with the 413 K comparison template (pressure difference, scale 1). It was excluded from the fit and is above the 368 K measured limit of the MDEA dissociation correlation. The pressure difference is 0.500 MPa. Kuranov's Experimental Section gives a maximum pressure uncertainty of 0.1% of the transducer's full-scale reading (at most 0.010 MPa even for its 10 MPa transducer) and an estimated temperature uncertainty of 0.1 K. The replay verifies the calculation. The 12 unfitted rows show departure from measured pressures within this campaign. [Kuranov row predictions and replay differences](results/kuranov-published-422/kuranov-rows.json) · [Input, script and wheel hashes](results/kuranov-published-422/hashes.json).

K19 and K32 each contain 35 fitted and six unfitted pressures. C28 has 22 fitted and six unfitted pressures, and C21 has 17 fitted and four unfitted pressures.

AARD is the mean absolute value of $100(p_\mathrm{calc}/p_\mathrm{exp}-1)$ (Uyan Eq. 25 and Wangler Eq. 32). The bias is the signed mean of the same pressure deviations. The reported maximum is absolute, with the source row in parentheses. The published target columns distinguish Uyan's 19.22% from §4.3.2 (39 rows inferred from the loading cutoff) and 19.82% from the abstract (41 rows inferred from the reported aggregate). Wangler's 32 wt% target is from Fig. 11, and the three 60 wt% observations are from Table 10 and Fig. 14 at 303.00 K.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import json
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import fmean
from tabulate import tabulate
results = Path("results/kuranov-published-422")
saved = json.loads((results / "statistics.json").read_text())
kuranov, wangler = [json.loads((results / file).read_text()) for file in ("kuranov-rows.json", "wangler-table-10-rows.json")]
current = [dict(subset=s, reading="Present model", printed=None, **v) for s, v in saved["present"].items()]
for reports in (current, saved["reconstruction"]):
    table = []
    for r in reports:
        subset, reading = r["subset"], r["reading"]
        cohort = [q for q in (wangler if subset == "Wangler Table 10" else kuranov) if q["source_row"] in saved["sets"][subset]]
        pressures = {q["source_row"]: q["present" if r["printed"] is None else reading]["pressure_Pa"] for q in cohort}
        dev = {q["source_row"]: 100 * (pressures[q["source_row"]] / q["p_exp"] - 1) for q in cohort if pressures[q["source_row"]] is not None}
        missing = sorted(pressures.keys() - dev.keys())
        aard, bias = (fmean(map(abs, dev.values())), fmean(dev.values())) if dev else (None, None)
        worst, maximum = max(((i, abs(d)) for i, d in dev.items()), key=lambda pair: pair[1], default=(None, None))
        full = None if missing else aard
        assert (len(cohort), len(dev), missing, full, aard, bias, maximum, worst) == tuple(r[k] for k in ("n", "solved", "unsolved_rows", "AARD_percent", "solved_AARD_percent", "bias_percent", "max_abs_percent", "worst_row"))
        table.append((subset, reading, r["printed"], f"{len(dev)}/{len(cohort)}", full, aard if missing else None, bias, f"{maximum:.4f} ({worst})" if dev else None, ", ".join(map(str, missing)) if missing else None))
    print(tabulate(table, headers=["Set", "Reading", "Printed (%)", "Solved", "AARD (%)", "Solved-row AARD (%)", "Bias (%)", "Max (%) and row", "Unsolved rows"], tablefmt="pipe", floatfmt=".4f", missingval="—", disable_numparse=[2]), end="\n\n")
```

The four retained readings use Uyan's Table 3 precision and Table 1 reaction constants, with the repository water and MDEA permittivity laws. The Uyan readings use Eqs. 26–27 with the Table 5 or zero water–MDEAH⁺ coefficient and the Table 5 water–MDEA association-volume correction. Both Wangler readings use Tables 6–7, interpreting the numbered temperature coefficients as powers. The charged-MDEA reading keeps its neutral packing diameter and self-dispersion, whereas the other three use $0.88\sigma$ for the ion packing diameter. None reproduces a printed target at the target's print resolution. The baseline Wangler reading yielded no pressure on the three 60 wt% rows from the specified starts. The charged-MDEA reading solved all three and underpredicted each measured pressure. The #126 Fig. 11 diagnostic showed the charged-MDEA curves up to 0.6 below the digitized curves in $\ln p$ at high loading. [The four fixed readings](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/422) · [Wangler Table 10 predictions and solve messages](results/kuranov-published-422/wangler-table-10-rows.json) · [Retained #126 Fig. 11 diagnostic](../mdea_kuranov_refit/results/wangler-figures-11-12.csv).

Raeispour Shirazi and Lotfollahi report **10.9% AARD** for their fitted ePC-SAFT-MB model (Str2, Table 4, p. 7). Their reference [44] and count identify the 82 Kuranov Table 2 total pressures. Section 5.3 states that two binary interactions were fitted to all 162 ternary bubble pressures, including these observations. Eq. 20 uses the same absolute relative pressure deviation. [Raeispour Shirazi and Lotfollahi source check](results/kuranov-published-422/raeispour-table-4.json).

These results await independent scientific review and investigator approval for manuscript use.

## Sensitivity to the shared water–bicarbonate interaction (#417)

The low and high MEA profiles qualified $k=0.1325000116847309$ and $k=1$ for transfer to MDEA. At these values the fitted MEA objective increased by 1.023004 and 0.023674, respectively, relative to the refitted center. The study tests how MDEA predictions and the finite phase-stability searches respond to the shared coefficient after each solvent refits its own parameters. [Study plan and selection rule](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/417).

### Fixed-coordinate MEA fits

The historical 11-coordinate F2 fit had $C=150.76290287953717$. The reported F2 parameters replayed at $C=150.76290287955263$ on Engine 1.3.1 `05e94210`, with all 307 fitted rows available. The relative change in objective was $1.03\times10^{-13}$, within the study's $10^{-10}$ replay limit. The maximum relative difference in a prediction was $2.02\times10^{-12}$. Refit at the full-precision center $k_0=0.7650000233694618$ gave $C(k_0)=150.76288471813868$. Its difference from the replay lies within the $10^{-6}C$ start-tie rule. The lower replayed refit cost sets the center for both profiles. [Control readback](results/shared-bicarbonate-417/control-readback.json).

The refits minimized $C(k)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^{307}r_i^2$ using the original weights, ten remaining F2 coordinates, two Born-to-segment-diameter ties, and two F2 start families. A candidate could increase the cost by at most 1.3986782374, the observed increase in the largest reported inward profile of the MEAH⁺–carbamate interaction. The two tested sides used the same allowance. The finite-search requirement was complete searches and no confirmed liquid–liquid split. Fits used only the fitted observations and kept $k$ fixed throughout.

| Fixed $k$ | Previous start, $C$ | Current start, $C$ | Lowest $C-C(k_0)$ | Outcome |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 0.7650000233694618 | 150.763064658 | 150.762884718 | 0 | Refitted center |
| −0.5 | 166.651406042 | 166.651406034 | +15.888521316 | Cost exceeds allowance |
| 0.1325000116847309 | 151.786667505 | 151.785889075 | +1.023004357 | First qualifying low value |
| 1.0 | 150.786558248 | 150.787225109 | +0.023673530 | First qualifying high value |

Every start converged and replayed all 307 fitted rows. The largest MEA endpoint replay difference was below the $10^{-8}$ relative cost check. The declared midpoints and quarter-distance values were computed from full-precision $k_0$. The low midpoint and high bound met the selection rule, ending the MEA profile at those points. ### MDEA refit and pressure and speciation comparisons

The bounded MDEA control replayed all 281 fitted rows at $C=564.48369612531$, within 4.71e-14 relative of the retained fit. At the selected MEA values the refitted MDEA costs were 541.079255 (low) and 565.942499 (high), with signed changes of -23.404441 and +1.458802. The high-minus-low span was +24.863243. [MDEA control rows](results/shared-bicarbonate-417/reported-mdea/replay.json.gz).

Each refit used the same eight MDEA coordinates, all three hash-identified starts, original observation weights, and the original bound on the MDEA–water coefficient at 423 K. Each start loaded the new fixed water–bicarbonate value before binding the model. The objective passed the $10^{-12}$ relative check when the MDEA–water interaction was written about 423 K. The selected start had the lowest converged objective on full replay. [Fitted mappings and start outcomes](results/shared-bicarbonate-417/mdea/).

### MDEA phase-stability searches

The CO₂-free checks used 1.466 MPa, the original 78 native searches, and the 1,041-composition hull scan. The onset comparison reused the hash-checked 33-temperature table after verifying the pure MDEA and water inputs. Each fitted temperature law was compared to the full table.

The binary contains no bicarbonate. Its result responds to refitting the MDEA–water law. The loaded-state and property comparisons describe sensitivity within the declared data, weights, bounds, local starts and sampled states. ## Bounded k(MDEA–water) fit without the CO₂-free gap (#411)

The owner adopted this set as the reported MDEA parameters on 23 November
2026, replacing the #343 interpolated set. All values use wheel 1.3.1 `05e94210`,
the #343 declaration, data roles and weights, and 4 worker processes.

**Cause of the interpolated result.** Of the eight free coordinates, only
k(MDEA–water) = a0 + a1 (T − T_ref) enters the CO₂-free binary. With every
other value fixed, the largest k without a gap in the lower convex envelope of
G/(RT) at 1.466 MPa (5,490 compositions, bisected to 10⁻⁶) rises almost
linearly from −0.13233 at 290 K to −0.06701 at 423 K, about
4.9×10⁻⁴ K⁻¹. The fitted slopes are 1.15–1.26×10⁻³ K⁻¹, so the hottest
penalty temperature binds. The #343 interpolated set has
k(423 K) = −0.0670122, 1.3×10⁻⁶ above that limit. Its finite penalty weight
let the optimizer accept 14 binary descents for about 100 units of data
cost, and the retreat then stopped on the onset line.
[Gap-onset table](results/bounded-binary-411/critical-k.json).

**Method.** The same linear law was written about T_ref = 423 K; the replay
cost of the interpolated set is unchanged to 10⁻¹². The no-gap requirement is
then the upper bound a0 ≤ −0.0671135 (onset minus 10⁻⁴). The fits use the
281 fitted rows only, with no penalty rows and no retreat. They start from
the two #343 retreated points and from the #343 scale-0.003 optimizer
endpoint, each moved onto the bound. A fourth fit from that endpoint
without the bound measures the cost of the requirement.
[Declaration](inputs/bounded-binary-411.json) ·
[Script](scripts/bounded_binary_411.py).

| Start | Bound | Iterations | Time (s) | Fitted-data cost | Active bounds | k(423 K) | Binary searches: available / descents | Hull gaps |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---|---|
| #343 retreated point, start 0 | yes | 11 | 501.8 | 564.483696 | k(423 K); k(MDEAH⁺–HCO₃⁻) = 1 | −0.067113 | 78 / 0 | none |
| #343 retreated point, start 1 | yes | 11 | 421.6 | 582.779688 | k(423 K); k(MDEAH⁺–H₂O) | −0.067113 | 78 / 0 | none |
| #343 scale-0.003 endpoint | yes | 6 | 140.3 | 564.483696 | k(423 K); k(MDEAH⁺–HCO₃⁻) = 1 | −0.067113 | 78 / 0 | none |
| #343 scale-0.003 endpoint | no | 40 + 35 | 720.3 | 479.442840 | none | −0.059940 | 77 / 14 | onset 413.05–413.15 K |

All four stopped on optimizer tolerance (the unbounded fit after one
continuation). The first and third bounded fits reach the same point:
costs agree to 8×10⁻¹² relative and every coordinate to 4.2×10⁻⁶ relative
(largest absolute difference 5.60×10⁻⁵ K, in $u_{\mathrm{MDEAH^+}}/k_B$). The
second stops at a separate minimum. At the selected point, k(T) is below
the onset value at all 33 tabulated temperatures from 290 to 423 K. The
binary searches are the 78 #343 states at 1.466 MPa; the hull scan uses
1,041 compositions at 32 temperatures from 288.71 to 422.04 K.
[Fit reports and endpoints](results/bounded-binary-411/fits/) ·
[Selected endpoint](results/bounded-binary-411/endpoint.json).

**Result.** A converged set without the CO₂-free gap at the tested states
exists. It is not the unbounded local minimum: from the same start, the unbounded fit
has a 15.1% lower fitted-data cost (479.44 versus 564.48) and places the
MDEA–water binary in a two-liquid region from about 413 K at 1.466 MPa.
Within this model form, removing the gap costs about 85 units of fitted-data
cost. This is a local comparison from one start, not a global bound.

0.17311–0.98067 of assigned to calculated pressure. The largest conditional correlation is 0.925, between

## Fixed-pressure CO₂-free stability penalty (#343)

The [18 November owner decision](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/343#issuecomment-6995164177)
adds CO₂-free MDEA–water to the #255 stability penalty. The four Kuranov
binary pressures and their group weights remain as described in the
unpenalized study below. The full #337 search and its loaded-state penalty
remain separate from the initial binary fit.

The added set contains **78 single-liquid parents** at **1.466 MPa**. The
temperatures are 393, 403, 413, 413.15, 422.04 and 423 K. The 10 K steps
cover the requested interval. The additional temperatures align with the
hot Kuranov data and the hottest declared Merkley state. MDEA mole fractions
are 0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.06, 0.07, 0.08, 0.10, 0.12, 0.14, 0.16, 0.18,
0.20 and 0.24. The 0.07 point samples the narrow gap found at 413.15 K in
the previous calculation, and 0.24 brackets its predecessor's upper contact
near 0.236 at 422.04 K. Each native Full-search observation has unit weight.
The #255 penalty scales are 0.01 and 0.003. The fixed binary pressures use
no bubble-pressure reference and the binary has no reactions.
[Binary penalty declaration](inputs/retransfer-343-binary-penalty.json).

The untouched fitted B1 endpoint still refuses the two 413.15 K Kuranov
pressures at the revised objective. Under the **19 November orchestrator
decision**, the substituted start is **B1 with k(MDEA-water) taken from start 2**.
It uses intercept −0.1797272203 at 313.15 K and slope
6.168324014e−4 K⁻¹. Every other value in the source parameter document
was verified equal to B1 before applying the unchanged shared-input binding
and Born-diameter tie. B1 remains the frozen comparison model.
[Repair provenance](results/retransfer-343/binary-penalty/repaired-start-provenance.json).

### Density roots of the loaded-state descents

At the retreated point from **B1 with k(MDEA-water) taken from start 2**,
the 77 records with descent evidence represent 28 distinct calculations.
The 27 distinct rule (a) cases descend toward vapor. One rule (b) grid case
has a resolved liquid–liquid split. The search summary preserves the 52
preliminary data-state labels based on trial seeds and records the final
counts separately under the density-root classification.

| Source | Trial phase identified at the parent pressure | Requested records | Distinct calculations |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Rule (a) data, native and supplied | Vapor | 64 | 24 |
| Rule (a) data, supplied only | Vapor | 12 | 3 |
| Rule (b) grid, native | Second liquid | 1 | 1 |

Replaying the native search reproduced the stored witness compositions.
For the 52 records labelled mixed in the original search, the density
solver's `root_density_side` was unspecified. The recorded `density_side`
fell back to the trial seed label. For each liquid-labelled witness, a
vapor-labelled witness matches its composition and log density within
$3.07\times10^{-12}$, below the Engine's `PHASE_COINCIDENCE_DISTANCE` of
$10^{-6}$. Requesting both density branches returned the same root.
On a 33-point isotherm at each trial composition, from $10^{-4}$ times
that root density to the root, pressure increased monotonically and every
sampled pressure derivative was positive. This identifies a
vapor-connected root at the sampled conditions. The rule (a) parent
pressures were 0.1733 to 0.9990 times their model bubble pressures.
[Native branch identification](https://github.com/tannerpolley/epcsaft/blob/05e94210fa64cf69725e45babc0411d32139df5a/engine/native/equilibrium/phase_stability.cpp#L165).

The evaluation-only supplied trials preserve their trial density and can be
off pressure. Across the 76 rule (a) records, 12,142 of 77,491 negative
evaluations already met the $10^{-10}$ parent pressure-row tolerance.
All 12,142 were vapor-side or connected to dilute gas at fixed composition.
The other 65,349 values retain negative evidence at the evaluated points.
Their original densities do not establish a pressure-equilibrated phase.
For each state's most negative trial, closing pressure at unchanged
composition gave a vapor-side root (24 records) or a vapor-connected
single root (52 records). Ten of those original trial densities needed
pressure closure. All density corrections remained within the native
`DENSITY_ANCHOR_LOG_WINDOW` of 0.00995033, with a maximum absolute log
density change of 0.00173223. At the closed roots the dimensionless
tangent-plane distances ranged from −1.61176 to −0.000992521. Each
negative magnitude exceeded its native numerical error estimate by at
least $7.54\times10^{6}$. These trials add vapor-side evidence and leave
the number of observed liquid–liquid splits at one.
The per-state `outside_ranges` field uses the #337 convention. A false
mark means the applicable law is within its source range, a true mark
means it is outside, and an unused reaction is identified explicitly.
The two 388.71 K states, `comparison:374:1:phase` and
`Merkley-capped:8:phase`, lie above the 368 K MDEA dissociation limit.
[All 77 records with temperatures, pressures, tangent-plane distances and range marks](results/retransfer-343/binary-penalty/descent-and-penalty-diagnosis/descent-states.csv) ·
[Pressure-root checks and witness compositions](results/retransfer-343/binary-penalty/descent-and-penalty-diagnosis/phase-witnesses.json).

The grid split is a predicted liquid–liquid equilibrium at 363.15 K,
78.620 wt% MDEA on the unloaded stock basis, 1.368 mol CO₂ per mol MDEA,
and 262.862 MPa (1.05 times the model bubble pressure). The native
liquid-side tangent-plane distance was −0.00262223. The seed yielded a
finite Gibbs decrease of $-2.89\times10^{-5}$ mol in $G/(RT)$, with
estimated numerical error $7.66\times10^{-10}$ mol on that feed basis.
A separate two-liquid equilibrium solve at the same conditions gave
molar densities of 22,332 and 24,983 mol/m³ and CO₂ mole fractions of
0.282 and 0.726. The second liquid accounts for 0.874% of the equilibrium
fluid moles. The maximum classified equilibrium residual was
$2.92\times10^{-14}$ against the Engine's $10^{-10}$ row tolerance.
Bulk $G/(RT)$ fell by $4.51\times10^{-5}$ mol on 3.918 mol feed.
This establishes a local model equilibrium at a highly concentrated,
high-pressure grid point. No measured coexistence was used to verify it.
The 1,039 unavailable searches remain unavailable and the split count
remains a lower bound.
[Two-liquid equilibrium calculation](results/retransfer-343/binary-penalty/descent-and-penalty-diagnosis/two-liquid-equilibrium.json).

### Pressure interpretation at the vapor-directed data states

At the 24 distinct data-state calculations with native vapor-directed
descent, the declared pressure was below the model bubble pressure.
The negative tangent-plane distance rules out the homogeneous liquid
as the stable equilibrium **at that declared pressure**. This is
consistent with vapor formation below the model bubble pressure.
The reported bubble pressures are local incipient-vapor roots solved
at higher pressures. The descents at the data pressures neither verify
nor rule out stability of those roots at their own pressures. Stability
of the reported bubble roots remains unverified. These searches concern
density, speciation and heat declarations. They identified no affected
Kuranov, Xiao or Ermatchkov pressure-observation rows.

| Data declaration | Distinct native-descent calculations | Affected rows or search records |
|---|---:|---|
| Sobrino unloaded density, fitted | 4 | `fit:200`, `fit:206`, `fit:212`, `fit:218` |
| Böttinger speciation at 5 bar, not fitted | 8 | `comparison:221–222`, `225–226`, `249–250`, `305–306`, `321–322`, `325–326`, `353–354`, `357–358` |
| Böttinger speciation at 25 bar, not fitted | 2 | `comparison:163–164`, `227–228` |
| Zheng integral heat, not fitted | 5 | Final states of `comparison:411`, `413–416` |
| Merkley heat and capped states, fitted and not fitted | 5 | `fit:126` (also `Merkley-capped:4:phase`), `comparison:370`, `comparison:374`, `Merkley-capped:5:phase`, `Merkley-capped:8:phase` |

These three-worker projections use the retained stratified compressed-row
sample and the measured 78 binary rows at the same endpoint. A row shared
by data and grid belongs to the data set in this accounting. Seven capped
sources still have no constructed compressed copies at either ratio. The
table estimates penalty evaluation time at a fixed parameter point.
Parameter-dependent work, optimizer cache reuse, fitted-data evaluations,
retreat and endpoint searching are outside the time calculation.

On the 127 available compressed sample rows, timings averaged 46.2 ms
per worker for the bubble reference solve, 62.2 ms for that solve with its
derivatives, 9.2 ms for the fixed-pressure reacting parent solve and
118.8 ms for its native tangent-plane search. The native fixed-pressure
row took 128.8 ms with 152.0 ms for prediction and derivatives together.
Independent call timings have distinct compilation and warm-up costs.
At the grid split, freezing pressure changes a dimensionless prediction
derivative by 0.1534 per optimizer unit, even though the central value
matches. Sharing an identical bubble-pressure reference between the
two ratios preserves both the predictions and residual Jacobian exactly.
Across 36 timed pair repetitions, separate evaluations took 13.273 worker
seconds and paired evaluations took 11.502 worker seconds, a 13.3%
reduction. The pinned fit already assigns identical references to the same
worker and reuses the solve. The measured gain applies to these pairs.
[Timed calls and stage projections](results/retransfer-343/binary-penalty/descent-and-penalty-diagnosis/timing.json).

All three original pressure-reference failures occur before applying the
compression ratio. Their largest classified residuals are material
balances. Four alternate pressure guesses per case still refused. At
313.15 K, neighboring converged starts also failed for the 78.620 wt%
stock at loading 0.8 and the approximately 43.4 wt% stock at loading 1.3.
The neighboring attempts reached a packing-domain or vapor-root
refusal. At 373.15 K and approximately 65.1 wt% MDEA at loading 1.3,
two neighboring seeds independently recovered a bubble pressure of
106.826642 MPa with residual $2.27\times10^{-13}$. This establishes a
start-sensitive solve for that row. The other two bubble references
remain unavailable under the tested starts.
[Exact refusal messages and independent starts](results/retransfer-343/binary-penalty/descent-and-penalty-diagnosis/bubble-pressure-refusals.json).

The #255 MEA records give 1,367 and 4,314 s for whole fits with 1,903
penalty parents and 32 requested workers. Normalizing those whole-fit
times by the penalty-row count and by the sum of the reported residual and
Jacobian evaluations gives 15.3–20.5 ms wall time per row per evaluation.
The same normalization gives 64.4–97.8 ms for the later #282 MEA stages
on three workers with the same enforced set. MDEA's weighted sample gives
110.8 ms per loaded row for residual evaluation and 127.3 ms for the
Jacobian on three workers. The MEA whole-fit records include the fitted
data and optimizer work. They cannot isolate native per-row time or a
same-wheel speed ratio. Adopted F2 in #338 needed no penalized stage.
[Historical fit references and accounting](results/retransfer-343/binary-penalty/descent-and-penalty-diagnosis/timing.json).

### OWNER DECISION 2026-11-19

The owner answered through the question tool to report the one
liquid–liquid split and retain the binary-penalty result without a
loaded-penalty refit. The split is outside the measured domain at
363.15 K, 78.620 wt% unloaded MDEA, 1.368 mol CO₂ per mol MDEA and
262.862 MPa, with TPD/$RT$ of −0.00262. The sample timings project
**14.1–20.2 h per stage** for the whole penalty set and **1.0–1.4 h**
for the data states alone (1.009–1.432 h before rounding).
Both exceed the one-hour limit. No loaded-penalty refit was run.
This is an owner-approved exception for MDEA only. The #337 series
penalty rule remains in force for the other amines.

## Previous unpenalized MDEA fit with CO₂-free Kuranov pressures (#343, 18 November 2026)

The fit stopped at the binary miscibility check. At the only fitted endpoint,
a liquid–liquid gap first appeared between **413.052 and 413.150 K** in the
sampled liquid Gibbs-energy calculation at **1.466 MPa**. At **422 K** the
sampled contact compositions were **0.029 and 0.140 mol MDEA/mol mixture**.
The optimizer reached its 40-iteration limit. The stop condition in the
[owner's decision](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/343#issuecomment-6961718041)
takes precedence over continuations and the full stability search. No endpoint
was selected.

### Measurements and weights

The four CO₂-free pressures below come from Kuranov et al. (1996), Table 2,
printed p. 1960, checked against the current Zotero attachment. The printed
column is ten times the total pressure in MPa. The source states maximum
pressure uncertainty of 0.1% of the transducer full scale (Experimental
Section, p. 1959) and temperature uncertainty of 0.1 K. The fit evaluates
all four as nonreactive binary bubble pressures. The two 413.15 K rows were
previously not fitted, the 393.17 K row exceeded B1's calculation interval,
and the 393.15 K row moved from the loaded-state declaration. Each Kuranov
stock has two rows at weight 0.5 each. The 58 Kim MDEA–water mixture rows use
weight 1/58 each, replacing their unit row weights. The three separate Kim
pure-water rows retain unit row weights. This gives each of the two Kuranov
stocks and the Kim mixture series total weight 1. Other weights and the
pressure log-ratio residual definition follow the retained declarations.
[Source transcription and weights](results/retransfer-343/kuranov-transcription.json).

| T (K) | MDEA (mol/kg water) | Measured pressure (kPa) | Predicted pressure at the stopped endpoint (kPa) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 393.17 | 1.9493 | 190.9 | 194.396 |
| 393.15 | 3.9707 | 186.2 | 192.482 |
| 413.15 | 1.9493 | 346.4 | 354.144 |
| 413.15 | 3.9707 | 338.6 | 353.477 |

At 413.15 K the two fitted homogeneous-liquid pressure predictions differ by
0.667 kPa. The measurements differ by 7.8 kPa. The bubble calculations follow
each specified liquid composition. The Gibbs-energy calculation below tests
whether two liquids can lower the energy at fixed temperature and pressure.
Neither calculation supplies experimental liquid–liquid coexistence data.
[Source and phase-rule interpretation](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/397#issuecomment-6961702192).

The Engine refused the B1 start with liquid curvature eigenvalues
−1.69456e−4 and −0.108859 at 1.9493 and 3.9707 mol/kg water, respectively.
Their negative rounding bands were approximately −2.11e−14 and −1.95e−14.
All 281 fitted rows replayed at the second start. Its initial binary screen
found no gap through 422.04 K at 1.466 MPa on the stated grid. The fit used
40 residual evaluations and 15 Jacobian evaluations. The retained history
includes 26 rejected trial costs represented by the largest finite double.
Of the recorded evaluation refusals, 24 report local liquid instability and
two report an infeasible saturation solve at a loading of 1.05 mol CO₂/mol MDEA.
[First start](results/retransfer-343/start-0/diagnosis.json),
[second start](results/retransfer-343/start-1/diagnosis.json),
[fit history and refusals](results/retransfer-343/start-1/unpenalized/stage-0/fit.json).

At the fitted endpoint the water–MDEA interaction is
$k=-0.1925744674 + (1.201976\times10^{-3}\;\mathrm{K}^{-1})(T-313.15\;\mathrm{K})$.
At 422 K, $k=-0.0617394$. The earlier estimate of a maximum slope near
$1.27\times10^{-3}\;\mathrm{K}^{-1}$ used the B1 intercept −0.20633735.
The endpoint has a less negative intercept. A slope bound for a revised fit
requires a corresponding intercept condition. [Previous diagnosis](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/397#issuecomment-6961702192).

The numerical miscibility check evaluates the homogeneous liquid branch at
1.466 MPa, the declared hot Merkley pressure, on 1,041 composition points
per temperature. It compares $\sum_i x_i[\ln x_i+\ln\phi_i]$ to its lower
convex envelope. Subtraction of pure-component reference terms would add a
linear function of composition and leave the comparison unchanged. The
central composition step is 0.001, with refined points near the pure ends.
An onset bracket narrowed the first detected gap to 0.1 K in temperature.
The contact values below are sampled compositions. Coexistence at other
pressures and intervals between the sampled temperatures remain unexamined.
[Binary miscibility calculation](results/retransfer-343/start-1/unpenalized/stage-0/binary-mixing.json).

## Current B1 adoption (#302, 11 November 2026)

The owner adopted the #298 **B1-endpoint** on the #255 shared values and complete R2 declaration in a [post-hoc owner amendment](https://github.com/tannerpolley/Amine-Thermodynamics/issues/298#issuecomment-6806627180). The original design did not pass every gate. A3 remains unrefit in `solvent_specification_mdea/A3.toml`; its old parameters are inconsistent with the adopted shared set. The A3 refit is retained only as evidence of the MEA → MDEA transfer penalty and is not adopted.

- F2 originally failed both A3 pressure comparisons. The owner treats Xiao's +0.27 percentage point as a measurement-level difference, citing ±1.5% pressure uncertainty. Ermatchkov's +5.23 percentage points remains a systematic loss. B1 passed both pressure comparisons.
- F3 originally failed Carson for B1 (1.132420 × historical scaled RMS, above 1.10) and A3 (1.103341 ×). The owner accepted B1 at scaled RMS 1.106 versus historical 0.977, comparable to accepted A3 historical 1.075.
- The two A3 388.71 K, 60 wt% Merkley heat failures are reported as concentration extrapolations beyond the intended ≤50 wt% domain, rather than gate failures.

The adopted specification replays 278 fitted predictions with maximum relative difference **0**, and cost **374.5190788052401** versus **374.5190788051367** (relative difference **2.7600e-13**). Xiao pressure AARD is **28.1910414167%** (20 rows); Ermatchkov is **18.2705616155%** (88 rows). This is numerical verification and conditional outside-fit assessment on wheel `391dfe5d`, SHA-256 `0962e21d2fa7a8ba1ed4622f1110b3e8053bacd878fa41c999d85e8b9afab66b`; it does not establish new physical validation.

Limits: two active bounds (protonated-MDEA–bicarbonate +1 and Born diameter 7 Å); conditional parameter uncertainty reported in the [adopted-specification notebook](../solvent_specification_mdea/notebook.qmd#parameter-uncertainty-and-sensitivity-307); no F4 phase evidence at 394.94–395.00 K; Kuranov rows 28 and 72 and seven corrected-Kamps states outside the adopted R2 domain; B1 333.15 K / 60 wt% heat unavailable. The retained F4 check covers 775 required records, with zero dense-liquid, ambiguous or unresolved states. No absorber-use qualification is claimed.

[Adoption replay](../solvent_specification_mdea/results/adoption-302/verification.json) and [explicit original verdicts and amendment](results/refit-298/disposition.json) retain the evidence. The sections below describe historical studies under their own parameter and wheel bindings.


## Outcome and intended use

The declared comparison between gate-passing starts within 1% of the selected cost passes: A1's 88-row Ermatchkov AARD is 26.208496003%, versus 26.208406176% for A3. The absolute difference is 0.0000898275 percentage points, below the non-identification threshold of 2 percentage points or more. B1 has no qualifying alternative: B3 fails the phase gate, and B2 duplicates B1. This check concerns agreement of pressure predictions between starts; it does not establish identification of individual parameters. The [eligibility and comparison record](results/stage2-capped/equal-cost-starts.json) and [88 A1 row predictions](results/stage2-capped/A1/ermatchkov-88.json) retain the numerical evidence.

Variant A fails the declared 24.2% pressure-transfer test; Variant B passes. AARD is average absolute relative deviation. The endpoints were selected by the lowest fitted cost among candidates passing the density-classified phase gate. Selection was committed in `005f79e` before any outside-fit statistic for the new capped endpoints was computed.

![Variant A exceeds the declared pressure limit; Variant B is below it. Points are aggregate statistics over 88 retained source rows, not an uncertainty estimate.](results/stage2-capped/transfer-test.png)

The pressure test uses all 88 Ermatchkov rows at ≤49 wt% MDEA, including the 29 rows below 7 kPa. The 13 higher-concentration rows and the complete 33-row low-pressure subset are separate comparisons. Nitrogen headspace is not modeled. These are conditional physical assessments of the declared model against outside-fit data. Fitted errors are calibration evidence; phase searches, derivative comparisons and balances are numerical verification. There is no absorber-use qualification or universal-ion-parameter claim.

## Model, inputs and selection

The liquid contains water, CO₂, MDEA, MDEAH⁺, bicarbonate, carbonate, hydronium and hydroxide; only neutral species enter the vapor. Variant A uses the MEA single-sphere cation convention; Variant B uses the charged-molecule convention. The shared MEA components, interactions and reaction laws remain frozen in the main fits. The MDEA–water interaction is linear in temperature, initialized from the Kim pre-fit. Neumann ideal-gas Cp is primary, with Wangler evaluated at the same endpoints as a sensitivity. Carson is integral heat from zero loading at 101325 Pa; Jakobsen scales are 10% of each observed ratio; Böttinger is evaluated at 5 and 25 bar.

Merkley uses the native Engine observable with final loading equal to the smaller of the digitized loading point and model saturation loading at 1121 kPa (1466 kPa for the 422.04 K source rows). Only the 20/40 wt% rows at 333.15 and 388.71 K enter the objective. The reaction domain remains 293.15–395 K; the 288.71/422.04 K Merkley and 413 K Kuranov comparisons are retained as unevaluated domain refusals. The source-loading digitization uncertainty is ±0.02 mol CO₂/mol MDEA. Above Hsieh's 328.15 K, the dielectric temperature dependence is a model assumption. The intended comparison domain is ≤49 wt% for the pressure test and ≤50 wt% for other properties; 60 wt% is extrapolation.

A1, A3, B1 and B3 all converged. A2/B2 are duplicates, and A4 remains excluded. B3 has one unresolved phase record (`comparison:113:0`) and is inadmissible for selection. A1 and A3 have costs differing by less than 1e-8; the declared exact lowest-cost rule selects A3. Active bounds are accepted under the owner's MEA precedent and do not establish that these quantities are experimentally identified.

When a control passes, the declared margin is two AARD percentage points, with the other property results retained; corrected Kamps is excluded. No MDEA outcome falsifies the MEA bicarbonate value, whose MEA conditional uncertainty already spans the declared range.

## Additional sources at the frozen endpoints {#sources-225}

Xiao's 20 equilibrium measurements give CO₂ partial-pressure AARDs of **20.40% at A3** and **28.28% at B1** at 23.5 wt% unloaded MDEA and 298.15–313.15 K.
The source is outside the fitted datasets.
These additional-source comparisons change neither the 24.2% Ermatchkov criterion nor its verdict: A fails and B passes.
No parameters were fitted and no manuscript result is revised.

| Source and quantity | Rows | A3 AARD (%) | B1 AARD (%) | Conditions and disposition |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Xiao Table 4, CO₂ partial pressure | 20 | 20.397551 | 28.276415 | 23.5 wt%, 298.15–313.15 K, 8.1–60.8 kPa |
| Ermatchkov primary CO₂ partial pressure, retained #222 statistic | 88 | 26.208406 | 19.146012 | ≤49 wt%; unchanged |
| Zhang equilibrium pressure/loading | 16 conditions | Unscored | Unscored | 5 mol/L single MDEA; extrapolation; numerical loadings and conversion density unavailable |
| Derks Table 1, species concentrations | 4 | Unscored | Unscored | 2 kmol/m³ initial MDEA; numerical temperature unavailable |

For Xiao, the calculation follows the #222 bubble-state pressure path at each measured loading and uses $p_{\mathrm{CO_2}}=P y_{\mathrm{CO_2}}$.
The logarithmic residual is $r_i=\ln(p_{i,\mathrm{model}}/p_{i,\mathrm{observed}})$; the reported AARD is $100 N^{-1}\sum_i |\exp(r_i)-1|$, rather than a percentage of logarithms.
The mean absolute log ratios are 0.239241 at A3 and 0.354606 at B1.
All 20 predictions are available at each endpoint, with requested equilibrium tolerances met.
The unloaded MDEA mass fraction is the printed 0.235; the printed rounded molality 2.58 mol/kg water is retained separately.
The experiments used CO₂/N₂ at 0.101 MPa; the model omits nitrogen, as in the Ermatchkov comparison.
These are conditional model predictions compared with measured pressures, not absorber-use qualification.
Source uncertainty is retained without treating it as parameter uncertainty or propagating it into an AARD confidence interval.

![Frozen endpoint predictions mostly underpredict Xiao's CO₂ partial pressures across the measured loading range. Points show predictions only at measured loadings; observation error bars are the source standard uncertainties, ±0.004 mol/mol loading and 1.5% pressure. Temperature and composition uncertainties are not displayed.](results/context-sources/Xiao-pressure.png)

The same #222 phase search was applied to each scored bubble state: reacting liquid on all eight species, vapor trials on neutral species, packing-fraction threshold 0.10, and the retained ambiguity interval 0.05–0.35.
At A3 and B1 separately, **20/20 states pass**, with **zero dense-split states, zero gas-evolution states, zero ambiguous states and zero unresolved states**.
No support-reconstruction failures occurred.
Gas evolution is counted separately and is not a dense-liquid failure.
These searches provide numerical evidence for the model's phase assumption at the scored states; they do not establish experimental phase stability or exhaustive global stability.
No phase search is claimed for unscored Zhang or Derks states.

### Source identities, transcription and unavailable quantities

Xiao et al. (2018), DOI 10.1016/j.jct.2018.03.020, **Table 4 and footnote, printed p.175 (PDF p.6)**, supplies all 20 rows in [the transcription](../../data/reference/MDEA/Xiao2018_context.csv).
The full 13-page PDF is attachment **C3NAG687**, SHA-256 `7c33012580b85fc940b0efe54380ee65c1745077382c41cd8605c309171f9975`, under new parent **6H2LM5C5**.
Old parent **WE7ZG7KW** retains first-page attachment **F3EC6J42**.
The footnote states standard uncertainties: pressure 1.5%, temperature 0.1 K, loading 0.004 mol CO₂/mol amine, unloaded MDEA 0.1 wt%, CO₂ 0.04 wt% and molality 0.01 mol/kg water.
The printed source-model loading and deviation columns are retained without using them as observations.

Zhang et al. (2023), DOI 10.1016/j.cej.2023.143279, **§2.2 (PDF p.2), §3.3 and Figures 6–9 (PDF pp.6–8)**, specifies 5 mol/L single MDEA and equilibrium experiments at 298, 303, 313 and 323 K, each at 5, 14, 30 and 60 kPa CO₂ partial pressure.
All 16 conditions per endpoint remain [explicitly unscored](results/context-sources/unscored-states.json).
The equilibrium loadings are graphical, not tabulated; main Tables 1–3 contain correlation coefficients.
The [author supplement at CNR](https://iris.cnr.it/handle/20.500.14243/439094), SHA-256 `8488f03dfdb693095b038d53c41a2ea1e8df70abc17d701d63002687498d38b1`, has four pages and supplies **Table S2, p.2**: [eight transient pure-MDEA rows](../../data/reference/MDEA/Zhang2023_context_transient.csv), including the unloaded row, with time, loading and species amounts in mol for 80 mL at 298 K.
These are time-dependent absorption measurements, not equilibrium pressure observations.
The paper's endpoint criterion is loading unchanged for two hours within ±0.002 C/N, with duplicate maximum deviation from the mean below 1%; Table S2 has no per-row uncertainty.
No numerical unloaded-solvent density was found in the main paper or supplement to convert 5 mol/L to mass fraction.
The issue's “about 57 wt%” remains a domain designation, not a substituted conversion datum.
Every prospective Zhang comparison is **extrapolation** beyond the 49/50 wt% domain.
No correlation-generated loadings or assumed density were substituted for observations.
The full 10-page PDF is **DJURMPCM**, SHA-256 `b29bc0ee96ad0695b1673dd4056d1c8cc7fb9cf7a0efed98ce6393935bb2d24e`, under new parent **PYMWILJ7**; old parent **TMHPSMM9** retains first-page attachment **PU7B5G27**.
The downloaded supplement has no Zotero attachment identity; no library item was changed.

Derks et al. (2011), DOI 10.1016/j.egypro.2011.01.094, **Table 1, printed p.603 (PDF p.5)**, supplies [four rows](../../data/reference/MDEA/Derks2011_context.csv) at loadings 0, 0.11, 0.42 and 0.80 mol CO₂/mol MDEA.
Parent **48VSQYEE**, attachment **5467GXJK**, SHA-256 `b646d4caafe53705d0b064698061f487fdc7f87d6e23908b6b31fb8029738582`, identifies the seven-page PDF.
The initial solvent is aqueous 2 kmol/m³ MDEA, and all three species columns are concentrations per liquid volume in kmol/m³.
Printed ± entries are retained, including zeros; the source does not state their confidence level.
The experimental description (§2, pp.600–602), abstract and Table 1 give ambient or room temperature without a numerical value.
Thus the volume-concentration basis is identified, but a numerical temperature and a density-based conversion to the model feed remain unavailable.

## Shared bicarbonate sensitivity and the Xiao pressure miss

At the frozen MDEA endpoints, reducing the bicarbonate–water interaction from
$k=0.7270558477497251$ to $0.6270558477497251$ improves Xiao agreement for both
cation representations. It improves the Ermatchkov comparison for the single
sphere A3 but worsens it for charged-molecule B1. The same change raises the
MEA 307-observation weighted cost from 148.879 to 157.930. These are conditional
parameter sensitivities, not an adopted shared value or evidence that the
cation representation alone controls the pressure error.

Xiao Table 4 supplies 20 measurements at 23.5 wt% unloaded analytical MDEA,
298.15–313.15 K and 8.1–60.8 kPa CO₂ partial pressure. The molality calculated
from that mass fraction is 2.57791 mol/kg water, consistent with the printed
2.58. Loading is moles of added CO₂ per mole of analytical MDEA. Section 3.2
and the table footnote identify CO₂/N₂ at 0.101 MPa total pressure. The
calculation retains the existing nitrogen-free bubble state and computes
$P y_{\mathrm{CO_2}}$. It therefore matches the reported quantity's label but
not the experiment's total-pressure state. Nitrogen and this pressure-state
difference remain unresolved; the results do not isolate an intrinsic
physical-model cause for the Xiao miss.

The live full Xiao PDF (Zotero `6H2LM5C5` / `C3NAG687`) matches the retained
SHA-256. Ermatchkov's current reading copy also matches the indexed Zotero
sidecar. Its Experimental Technique and Tables 1–3 establish the molality
basis for the 88 primary comparison rows. [Source checks and input hashes](results/transfer-267/source-basis.json)
record these findings. The four-reaction chemistry retains R1–R3 and the
MDEAH⁺ dissociation direction and reference convention. Uyan 2015 §3 and Table 1
supply the mole-fraction law; its molality conversion adds 4.0165 to $\ln K$.
It gives $pK_m=8.54994$ at 298.15 K, versus 8.55071 from the Kamps–Maurer law.
The [existing source comparison](results/reaction-basis-kamps-maurer.json)
attributes the small difference to printed coefficient rounding. Application
above the source's 368 K limit remains extrapolation. No chemistry law was
adjusted in these probes. Xiao's own modified Kent–Eisenberg model
(§2, Eqs. 1–15) correlates its effective dissociation constant with temperature
and physical CO₂ solubility. That fitted relation is not a replacement for
the retained thermodynamic dissociation law. These comparisons use the
experimental loading column, not Xiao's calculated loading column.

AARD is $100\langle|p_{\rm calc}/p_{\rm obs}-1|\rangle$; bias is the signed
mean of the same relative error. All 108 pressure states per probe returned
values. Their declared finite phase searches detected zero dense-liquid or
gas witnesses and zero unresolved states. This does not establish global
stability. The original pressure predictions replay within $10^{-8}$ relative
(or $10^{-8}$ Pa near zero).

| Representation and probe | Shared $k$ | Xiao AARD (%) | Xiao bias (%) | Ermatchkov AARD (%) | Ermatchkov bias (%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A3 baseline | 0.727056 | 20.3976 | −20.3976 | 26.2084 | −18.8835 |
| A3, $k-0.1$ | 0.627056 | 10.5526 | −3.3441 | 23.1772 | −1.3759 |
| A3, $k+0.1$ | 0.827056 | 34.4541 | −34.4541 | 34.7715 | −32.9226 |
| A3, retained joint refit | 0.294490 | 19.1954 | −18.6376 | 20.7305 | −5.7513 |
| B1 baseline | 0.727056 | 28.2764 | −28.2066 | 19.1460 | +0.8939 |
| B1, $k-0.1$ | 0.627056 | 16.4205 | −11.9838 | 27.2756 | +23.2050 |
| B1, $k+0.1$ | 0.827056 | 41.4631 | −41.4631 | 23.3225 | −16.9997 |
| B1, retained joint refit | −0.086756 | 30.0501 | −30.0501 | 32.5173 | −31.2243 |

Circles denote A3, squares B1; each point summarizes the retained source rows for one declared probe, without interpolation. Measurement and parameter uncertainty are not propagated.](results/transfer-267/pressure-comparison.png)

The retained joint refits also changed MDEA-specific coordinates. They do not
isolate bicarbonate sensitivity. The separate frozen-endpoint $k\pm0.1$
calculations do. The 24.2% Ermatchkov criterion is a repository assessment
limit, not experimental uncertainty. A3 at $k-0.1$ enters that limit; B1 at the
same shared value leaves it. None of these cases eliminates the negative Xiao
mean bias in both representations while meeting the Ermatchkov criterion for
both.

### Testing the active parameter bounds

One matched refit per representation uses the original fitted observations,
weights and scales, starting from the selected endpoint. Shared values remain
at the MEA baseline. Only four finite search limits change: cation–CO₂ and
cation–water constant $k$ use [−0.6, 0.6], cation–bicarbonate uses [−1.2, 1],
and Born diameter uses [1.5, 8] Å. The other limits and nine-coordinate
parameterization are unchanged. Native fitting retains the 40-iteration and
2100-second limits and the original tolerances.

These intervals test whether artificial search limits control the comparison;
they are not measured physical parameter ranges. Uyan 2015 Eq. 7 gives
$u_{ij}=\sqrt{u_i u_j}(1-k_{ij})$. Requiring nonnegative unlike attraction
excludes $k>1$ under that interpretation. Positive component energies and
diameters are also necessary conditions. They do not establish parameter
identifiability or physical validation. The cation–water temperature law is
checked at 293.15 and 395 K, the endpoints of this assessment interval.

The A3 fit converges in 13 iterations, with weighted cost 396.38810 versus
403.71499 at the original endpoint. Its Ermatchkov AARD is 20.43947%, with
+5.24458% bias; Xiao AARD is 20.96662%, with −19.66526% bias and 17/20
underpredictions. The cation–water $k=-0.6$, cation–bicarbonate $k=-1.2$ and
Born diameter 8 Å reach the expanded bounds. Its cation–water law remains
below 1 at both temperature endpoints. Thus expanding the box changes the
pressure comparison but does not remove bound dependence or the Xiao miss.
Its finite full-state phase search covers 754 states, detects 35 gas-evolution
witnesses, and detects no dense-liquid split or unresolved state. These gas
witnesses are distinct from the rejected dense-liquid phase condition. [Fit, replay and phase evidence](results/transfer-267/A3-bounds/)
retain every original fitted group, native trial failure and phase classification.

The B1 expanded-bound fit converges in 5 iterations at cost
373.17470, versus 374.45201 originally. Its Xiao AARD/bias remain
28.02791% / −27.95981%; Ermatchkov gives 18.99988% / +0.10828%.
Its 754-state finite phase search detects 36 gas-evolution witnesses, no
dense-liquid split, and no unresolved state. Cation–bicarbonate $k=1$ and
Born diameter 8 Å remain bound-active.
Extending the former beyond 1 would leave the adopted nonnegative unlike-attraction
interpretation. Neither fit isolates the cation, and the pressure ranking remains
reversed between the sources. These two finite box extensions do not support
an unrestricted statement about every admissible parameterization.

Every original fitted property group remains in the objective. Their weighted
costs are retained below; heterogeneous groups must not be compared as equally
weighted physical errors. Fresh native-prediction replays reproduce weighted
residuals within $10^{-8}$ absolute and cost within $10^{-8}$ relative.

### The missing 333 K heat

The charged-molecule B1 native saturation-capped heat at 333.15 K, 60 wt% MDEA,
1121 kPa and source loading cap 0.811 mol/mol remains unavailable after
refining the loading search from the original 30 samples to 60 and 120 samples
over the same 0.05–1.50 mol/mol bounds. The native diagnostic cannot admit a
vapor-density branch: at the original grid it finds a stable root at
33402.24 mol/m³ above a negative-slope sample at 10464.56 mol/m³, with an
unexamined gap and unresolved slope reversals. Finer loading sampling changes
the failing density values but does not resolve branch admission. This is a
numerical search limitation; it does not show that absorption heat is
physically undefined.

| Control, at 60 wt% and 1121 kPa | 30-sample heat (kJ/mol CO₂) | 60-sample heat | 120-sample heat |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A3, 333.15 K | −76.268595 | −76.268595 | −76.268595 |
| B1, 388.71 K | −64.128582 | −64.128582 | −64.128582 |

The controls' largest change is below $4\times10^{-9}$ J/mol CO₂. The separate
saturation diagnostic near 0.80691 mol/mol was not substituted for the native
observable. No complete two-observation B1 60 wt% heat AARD is calculated.
Sixty wt% remains a composition extrapolation. [The exact reproducer](results/transfer-267/heat-reproducer.json)
retains parameter documents, caloric and reaction declarations, all grids,
failure messages and the requested upstream check. The requested correction
must preserve the full-grid uniqueness check and both controls. The
[original wheel results](results/transfer-267/heat.json) separate the failure
from these useful control heat values.

The latest merged Engine main tested here is `4ffbb2b0825a28cdfa87dc333a586e641ff4c4b0`,
with wheel SHA-256 `40a58fc8f341f2ef4d9f26ae604cda93a5380e2a87073147bc2ba8efb17864b2`.
An unmodified archive of that fetched commit was built and installed in a separate
worktree environment. The [latest-wheel reproduction](results/transfer-267/heat-latest.json)
returns the same B1 333.15 K refusal on every grid. Both controls agree with the
original wheel within $1.4\times10^{-13}$ relative. The failure therefore persists
on that merged main commit. The combined [heat reproducer](results/transfer-267/heat-reproducer.json)
contains both wheel identities, all input documents, grids, outputs and the stated
correction criteria. The orchestrator owns the Engine request; this study has not
changed Engine source or adopted the diagnostic wheel.


For #255 stage 3, retain both cation representations and test the final MEA

bicarbonate decrease is a sensitivity direction for joint assessment, not a

## Issue 298: MDEA refits with the adopted shared MEA values

**The declared refits do not recover all required properties.** B1 recovers both pressure baselines; A3 recovers neither. Both selected records fail the Carson group-preservation rule. A3 also fails two outside-fit heat checks at 388.71 K and 60 wt% MDEA. This is the transfer penalty of the adopted shared set under this model, objective, bounds and declared starts, rather than a global impossibility result.

The historical costs reproduce after restoring the pre-0e216fe water ideal-gas calorics in scratch. The refits use current calorics and the pinned 391dfe5d wheel. Kuranov source rows 28 and 72 are excluded from both baselines and refits, leaving 278 fitted observations. The adopted R2 law is unchanged.

These are calibration and numerical verification results for the manuscript workflow comparison. They do not establish absorber suitability or parameter transferability. No parameters are adopted. Independent delivered-evidence review and investigator promotion remain pending.

### Limits and retained evidence


The two A3 outside-fit heat failures are concentration extrapolations at 388.71 K and 60 wt% MDEA. For the half-loading diagnostic, the calculated heat changes from −82.344969 to −85.682725 kJ/mol CO₂ against an observation of −63.3 kJ/mol, increasing absolute error by 3.337756 kJ/mol. For the capped integral heat, it changes from −74.141516 to −77.732589 kJ/mol, increasing absolute error by 3.591073 kJ/mol. Both increases exceed the permitted residual scale of 3.165 kJ/mol.

For B1 at 333.15 K, 60 wt% MDEA and 1.121 MPa, the capped heat remains unavailable at both baseline and refit: the original native search refuses the vapor branch at loading 1.45 mol/mol. No shortened grid or finite substitute heat is used, and no numerical heat-recovery claim is made for that row.

The two excluded Kuranov temperatures (393.17 and 393.16 K) exceed the adopted R2 upper limit of 393.15 K. No law was extended. Historical costs use 280 rows and are not directly comparable to the 278-row costs. Phase failure rejects an endpoint; unresolved numerical checks prevent a clean verdict. Neither establishes global impossibility of recovery. Active bounds and local Jacobian rank do not establish parameter identification. The 60 wt% comparisons remain concentration extrapolations. The original 30-node heat search over loading 0.05–1.50 mol/mol is preserved, including refusals. A historically unavailable B1 heat has no finite historical comparator.

F1.json owns qualification and provenance; attempts.json and each start directory own fit results; eligibility.json owns endpoint eligibility; selection.json freezes selection before pressure scoring; pressure-scores.json and gates.json own the comparisons. No source coefficients or Engine source were changed. The historical-water calculation is retained as logs/water-coefficient-confirmation.py and its row outputs, with coefficients recoverable from Git.

Execution: agent-heavy .venv/bin/python analyses/mdea_mea_workflow/scripts/continue_298.py runs the declared fits after historical confirmation; agent-heavy .venv/bin/python analyses/mdea_mea_workflow/scripts/assess_298.py runs the endpoint checks and assessments. The latter reuses retained phase calculations and applies the owner domain exclusion before freezing the selection.
